newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Japan PM says trusts Australia on car tariff cuts.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM says trusts Australia on car tariff cuts.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Tuesday he believed the Australian government would take Japan's investment in the local car industry into consideration when looking at tariff reductions.
Hashimoto said Japan's auto investment in Australia had created numerous jobs in Australia and also served as the lynchpin of the ties between Japan and Australia.

"So what I told Prime Minister Howard, in conclusion, on this matter was 'John, I trust you and I'm sure you will take into consideration these aspects as well and arrive at a balanced conclusion'," he said at a joint news conference with Australian Prime Minister John Howard. "Because I do believe that Prime Minister Howard is a very trustworthy person."

The Australian government is considering its response to draft recommendations from the Industry Commission that car tariffs should be continually reduced until they reached the general manufacturing protection rate of five percent.
The commission said this target should be reached by 2004, but the car industry has called for a freeze on tariffs after an initial reduction to 15 percent by 2000.
Hashimoto said tariff reduction was a common objective of all countries involved in the World Trade Organisation (WTO) and the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation Group (APEC).
"Essentially, this matter is a domestic affair of Australia," Hashimoto said.
"Trade liberalisation is a matter for common objective for all our countries under the WTO and APEC and something that we all must pursue actively."
The commission is due to release its final report on the car industry on May 26.
Toyota Motor Co and Mitsubishi Motor Corp both have manufacturing plants in Australia.
